mainTopic: Holiness of a female set aside for an אשם: its baby, selling it, and קדושת הגוף versus קדושת דמים
overview: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says that even רבי אלעזר agrees that the baby of a female set aside for an אשם is not brought as an אשם. The גמרא explains why this ruling is needed, and why it is said about an אשם and not about an עולה. Then a משנה rules that a female set aside for an אשם must graze until it gets a מום before it is sold. רבי שמעון says it may be sold right away. רב explains the first view with a מיגו: since קדושת דמים came onto the animal, קדושת הגוף came too. רבא first disagrees with רב כהנא about a male consecrated for its value, then changes his mind and agrees with him. רבי יוחנן explains that רבי שמעון holds that something unfit to be offered never gets קדושת הגוף. He backs this up with the case of an אשם brought at the wrong age. The גמרא answers a challenge from an animal that is too young, which רבי שמעון learns from a בכור. A new ברייתא about a female set aside for an עולה begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even רבי אלעזר agrees about a female set aside for an אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא rules that רבי אלעזר agrees: the offspring of a female set aside for an אשם is not brought as an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: רבי אלעזר agrees that if someone sets aside a female animal for an אשם, her baby is not offered as an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: A sage tells us where רבי אלעזר agrees with the חכמים. Someone set aside a female animal as an אשם, and her baby cannot be brought as an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that if a female was set aside for an עולה, her baby can be brought as an עולה. Here we learn that he does not say the same about an אשם, which must always be a male.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees (with the other opinion)
sets aside (an animal for a קרבן)
a female animal
a guilt offering, which is only brought from a male
her offspring, her baby

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
And Rabbi Elazar agrees
in a case where one sets aside a female for a guilt offering
that her offspring is not offered as a guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רבי אלעזר's ruling about a female set aside for an עולה, which was discussed earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to everyone, including רבי אלעזר, the offspring of a female set aside as an אשם is not offered as an אשם.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי אלעזר's reason applies only to an עולה, because a female can be an עולה. A female can never be an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious? רבי אלעזר only spoke about a female set aside for an עולה, because the name עולה can apply to a female like the mother. But a female can never be called an אשם, so of course even רבי אלעזר agrees the baby is not offered as an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא needed to say this at all. It seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's reason was that a female can still carry the name עולה, since bird עולות can be female. An אשם is never female, so that reason does not work here. So the ruling seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)
he only said this in the case of...
the name עולה can apply to a female like its mother
a burnt offering

phrases.english: It is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar only said his ruling
in a case where one sets aside a female for a burnt offering,
since there is a burnt offering status for its mother,
phrases.notes: A female can be an עולה in some cases, such as birds. So the name עולה can fit the mother.

phrases.english: but regarding one who sets aside a female for a guilt offering,
where there is no guilt offering status for its mother —
even Rabbi Elazar agrees
that it is not offered as a guilt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the statement in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר's known reason (the name עולה can fit a female) clearly does not apply to an אשם. So the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought רבי אלעזר's reason was different
steps.stepSummary: Without this ruling, we might have thought רבי אלעזר's reason was that the male baby is fit to be offered. That reason would apply to an אשם too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had not told us, I would have said that רבי אלעזר's reason is not that the mother can be called an עולה. I would have thought his reason is that the baby itself is fit to be offered. This baby is also fit to be offered. So he teaches us that it is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling is needed. We could have misunderstood why רבי אלעזר allows the baby to be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אלעזר's reason were 'the baby is a fit male', then the baby of the אשם mother should also be offered. The ruling shows that his real reason depends on the mother's status. Since a female can never be an אשם, his reason does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
the reason
fit to be offered on the מזבח
so he teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי אלעזר's ruling depends on the mother's status, not only on whether the baby is fit to be offered.

phrases.english: If he had not taught us,
I would have said that the reason of Rabbi Elazar

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּשֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: is not because there is burnt offering status for its mother,
but because the offspring is fit to be offered,
and this one too is fit to be offered,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the male baby of the female set aside for an אשם.

phrases.english: so he teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is needed to rule out a wrong reading of רבי אלעזר's reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's reason is that the male baby is fit to be offered, so the baby of an אשם mother would also be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: His reason is the mother's possible עולה status. That does not exist for an אשם, so the baby is not offered as an אשם.

steps.title: Why not teach the broader case of an עולה?
steps.stepSummary: If the point is to reject the 'fit baby' reason, the ruling should say the baby is not even offered as an עולה. Then we would know the same about an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of teaching us that her baby is not offered as an אשם, he should teach us that her baby is not offered as an עולה. The same would then be true for an אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. It asks why the ruling was said about an אשם and not in a way that would teach more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 was that the ruling rejects the 'fit baby' reason. If so, the broader way to reject it is to say the baby is not offered even as an עולה. That would seem to cover the אשם case too.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (if your answer is correct)
instead of teaching us...
and the same law applies

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּמַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאֵין בְּנָהּ קָרֵב אָשָׁם,
phrases.english: rather than teaching us that her offspring is not offered as a guilt offering,
let him teach us that her offspring is not offered as a burnt offering,
and the same would apply to a guilt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 3 and challenges the way the ruling was worded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to say the ruling about an אשם instead of an עולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'not offered as an עולה' would reject the 'fit baby' reason more broadly and would cover the אשם case too.

steps.title: A ruling about an עולה would not have covered the אשם
steps.stepSummary: Had he only taught about an עולה, we would have said that case is different, because the mother was never made holy as an עולה. For an אשם, where the mother was made holy as an אשם, we might have said the baby is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had taught us only about an עולה, I would have said: it is only as an עולה that the baby is not offered, because the mother was not made holy as an עולה. But as an אשם, since the mother was made holy as an אשם, I would say the baby is offered as an אשם. So he teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ruling had to be said about an אשם in particular. A ruling about an עולה would not have taught the אשם case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה ruling could be explained by a different reason: the baby's holiness would not match the mother's, since she was made holy as an אשם. With an אשם the holiness does match, so we might have allowed it. The ruling teaches that even then the baby is not offered.

keyTerms.meaning: he made it holy, consecrated it
the holiness of an עולה
since, because
I might say

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי אלעזר agrees that the baby of a female set aside as an אשם is not offered as an אשם. His reason in the עולה case is that a female can be an עולה, and that never applies to an אשם. The ruling had to name the אשם, because the baby's holiness matches the mother's there, and we might have allowed it.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'wrong assumptions' in this sugya. In step 3 the wrong idea is about רבי אלעזר's reason (the baby is a fit male). In step 5 the wrong idea is that matching holiness (אשם to אשם) would be enough.

phrases.english: If he had taught us about a burnt offering,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: עוֹלָה הוּא דְּלָא קָרְבָה,
phrases.english: I would have said: it is as a burnt offering that it is not offered,
because he did not consecrate its mother
with burnt offering sanctity,
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are in the printed גמרא but the corrected wording leaves them out. The square-bracket words are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: but as a guilt offering —
since he consecrated its mother as a guilt offering —
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: I might say: the offspring is offered as a guilt offering,
so he teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the אשם case teaches something an עולה case could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ruling about an עולה could be explained by the mismatch in holiness. Then an אשם baby, whose holiness matches the mother's, would be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when the holiness matches (אשם), the baby is not offered as an אשם, even according to רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The משנה: a female set aside for an אשם waits for a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that a female set aside for an אשם grazes until it gets a מום. Then it is sold and an אשם is bought with the money. If his אשם was already brought, the money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sets aside a female animal for an אשם, it grazes until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold, and he buys an אשם with the money. If his אשם was already offered, the money goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on what to do with a female animal that someone set aside for an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם can only be a male, so this female can never be offered. Still, it cannot be sold right away; it must first get a מום. Its value goes toward an אשם, or toward נדבה if he no longer needs one.

keyTerms.meaning: one who sets aside an animal for a specific קרבן
a female animal
it grazes until it becomes blemished
voluntary gift offerings

steps.confusionAlert: The female itself is never offered. It is waiting for a מום only so that it may be sold. The money is what gets used for the אשם.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sets aside a female for a guilt offering
it grazes until it becomes blemished
and it is sold, and he brings a guilt offering with its money
and if his guilt offering was already offered
its money goes to gift offerings

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה that deals with the same kind of case as the earlier discussion: a female set aside for an אשם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female set aside for an אשם must wait for a מום before being sold. The money buys an אשם, or goes to נדבה if his אשם was already brought.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: it may be sold without a blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and says the female may be sold right away, without waiting for a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: it may be sold without a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the other opinion in the משנה. He says there is no need to wait for a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a female can never be an אשם, רבי שמעון treats it as if it already has a blemish. So it may be sold immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: a physical blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
without a blemish

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
it may be sold without a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to the תנא קמא in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The female may be sold immediately, without a מום.

steps.title: Why wait for a blemish if the female is already unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא. A female can never be an אשם, so that unfitness should count as a מום, and it should be sold right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it to become blemished? Let it be sold now! Since it is not fit for what it was set aside for, that is the same as a blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא makes us wait for a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מום matters only because it makes an animal unfit for the מזבח. This female is already unfit, so the גמרא argues it should be treated as blemished now.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not fit for the purpose it was set aside for
that is the same as

phrases.english: GEMARA: And why do I need it to become blemished?
Let it be sold now!
Since it is not fit for the matter
phrases.notes: The matter is being offered as an אשם, which a female can never be.

phrases.english: that is the same as a blemish!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the תנא קמא in step 6, using the same reasoning as רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's requirement to wait for a מום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unfitness for the מזבח is the whole point of a מום. The female is already unfit, so waiting for a real מום seems pointless.

steps.title: רב: once value-holiness comes, body-holiness comes too
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the female does get קדושת הגוף. This comes through a מיגו: since קדושת דמים rested on it, קדושת הגוף rested on it too. An animal with קדושת הגוף may not be sold until it has a real מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the reason. We say that since holiness of value came onto it, holiness of the body came onto it too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers why the תנא קמא requires a מום. The animal's body itself became holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a female set aside for an אשם only has holy value, which would let it be sold right away. רב says that when value-holiness takes hold, body-holiness takes hold along with it. Body-holiness needs a real מום before the animal can be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: since; one result brings another along with it
holiness of value; only the animal's money worth is holy
holiness of the body; the animal itself is holy
came down onto it; took hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: The difference between קדושת דמים and קדושת הגוף is the key. Once קדושת הגוף is on an animal, it cannot be sold until it gets a real מום, even if it can never be offered.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the reason, for we say:
since holiness of value came onto it
holiness of the body came onto it as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ טַעַם דְּאָמְרִינַן מִיגּוֹ דְּנָחֲתָא לַהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reveals a hidden principle (מיגו) that explains the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the female can never be offered, it has only קדושת דמים and may be sold right away.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדושת דמים pulls קדושת הגוף along with it, so the animal must wait for a real מום.

steps.title: רבא: a male consecrated for its value gets body-holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from רב's principle that if someone consecrated a male only for its value, the animal still gets קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This means that if one consecrated a male for its value, it becomes holy with holiness of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws a new rule from רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a female, which can never be offered, gets קדושת הגוף from the מיגו, then a male surely does. A male is fit for the מזבח, so its body becomes holy even though the owner only meant to consecrate its value.

keyTerms.meaning: this means; a rule is being drawn from what was just said
he consecrated it for its value, meaning to sell it and use the money

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: consecrating an animal for its value alone still gives it קדושת הגוף, so the animal itself becomes holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far רב's מיגו reaches. A person cannot keep holiness on the money alone when the animal itself is fit for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rava said: That is to say,
if one consecrated a male for its value
it is holy with holiness of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new rule from רב's principle in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A male consecrated for its value gets קדושת הגוף.

steps.title: Male animal consecrated for its value: רב כהנא and רבא disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says a male animal consecrated only for its value gets קדושת הגוף. רבא says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if a person consecrated a male animal only for its money value, רב כהנא says it gets קדושת הגוף. רבא says it does not get קדושת הגוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement between two אמוראים about a male animal that someone consecrated only so it would be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male animal is fit to be brought as a קרבן, but the owner only meant its value to be holy. רב כהנא says the body becomes holy anyway. רבא says only the value is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated it for its value, meaning only its money worth is holy and it is meant to be sold
Holiness of the body itself, so the animal itself must be offered and cannot simply be sold
A male animal, which is fit to be an אשם or an עולה

phrases.english: It was stated: if one consecrated a male animal for its value,
phrases.notes: He means he wanted it sold so the money could buy a קרבן. He did not mean for the animal itself to be offered.

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף,
phrases.english: Rav Kahana says: it is holy with holiness of the body,

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: Rava says: it is not holy with holiness of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a formal מחלוקת on the same case that was drawn from רב's principle in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא: קדושת הגוף applies. רבא: it does not.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind and agrees with רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes back his view and agrees with רב כהנא, because of רב יהודה's quote from רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא changed his mind and agreed with רב כהנא, because of what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רבא later gave up his opinion and agreed with רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is רב's מיגו from step 9. Once קדושת דמים rests on an animal, קדושת הגוף rests on it too. That is even more true for a male, which is fully fit to be offered, so the final view is that it gets קדושת הגוף.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on his words, meaning he changed his mind

steps.whatToRemember: The final view is that a male animal consecrated only for its value still gets קדושת הגוף. This follows רב's מיגו.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at רבא's first opinion. He changed his mind, so in the end both אמוראים agree with רב כהנא.

phrases.english: And Rava retracted and agreed with Rav Kahana,
because of what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.
phrases.notes: This is the מיגו from earlier: since the holiness of value rested on it, the holiness of the body rested on it too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the מחלוקת of step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A male consecrated for its value gets קדושת הגוף, based on רב's מיגו.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי שמעון accept the מיגו?
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין asks רבי יוחנן why רבי שמעון lets the female אשם be sold without a מום. The מיגו should give it קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that רבי שמעון holds the female may be sold without a מום. רב חייא בר אבין asked רבי יוחנן: since קדושת דמים came onto it, קדושת הגוף should come onto it too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי שמעון's view in the משנה and challenges it using רב's מיגו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the מיגו is strong enough to give קדושת הגוף. If so, the female set aside for an אשם should also get קדושת הגוף, and then it could not be sold until it gets a real מום. So how can רבי שמעון let it be sold right away?

keyTerms.meaning: Since, meaning that because one thing happened, another thing happens along with it
Holiness of the value only, so the animal may be sold and the money is holy
Without a blemish

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תִּימָּכֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּמוּם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: it may be sold without a blemish.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 7 about the female set aside for an אשם.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Avin said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Since holiness of value came down onto it,
holiness of the body should also come down onto it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיגּוֹ דְּנָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים, תֵּיחוֹת לֵיהּ נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the מיגו we just established and uses it against רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that the female אשם may be sold without a מום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following רב's מיגו, קדושת דמים should bring קדושת הגוף along with it, and then the animal could not be sold without a מום.

steps.title: רבי שמעון holds that something unfit for the מזבח never gets קדושת הגוף
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that רבי שמעון follows his own view. Anything not fit to be offered itself cannot get קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning. He holds that anything not fit to be offered itself does not get קדושת הגוף.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. רבי שמעון does not accept the מיגו when the animal itself is unfit to be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מיגו only works if the animal could actually be offered. A female can never be an אשם, so in רבי שמעון's view קדושת הגוף has nothing to rest on. Only קדושת דמים applies, and so it may be sold right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, meaning this matches a view he holds elsewhere
Not fit in itself, meaning the animal cannot be brought as that קרבן

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, for he says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִידֵּי דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ לְגוּפֵיהּ —
phrases.english: anything that is not fit in itself —
holiness of the body does not come down onto it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the מיגו according to רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מיגו should apply to every animal that has קדושת דמים, including the female.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון the מיגו does not work when the animal itself cannot be offered, so the female gets only קדושת דמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the מיגו has a limit. It cannot create holiness of the body for something that could never go on the מזבח.

steps.title: The ברייתא: an אשם brought at the wrong age
steps.stepSummary: The proof starts. The תנא קמא rules that an אשם brought at the wrong age is valid, but it does not count for the owner's obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: an אשם that should be one year old but was brought at two years old, or one that should be two years old but was brought at one year old, is valid. But it does not count for the owner's obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what רבי שמעון holds. This first part gives the view of the תנא קמא and sets up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds the animal is still holy and may be offered, even though it does not fulfill the owner's obligation. This is the background that רבי שמעון will disagree with.

keyTerms.meaning: In its first year
Valid, meaning it may be offered
For the sake of his obligation, meaning counting as the קרבן he owes

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אָשָׁם בֶּן שָׁנָה וֶהֱבִיאוֹ בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: As it is taught: an אשם that should be one year old, and he brought it at two years old,
or one that should be two years old, and he brought it at one year old —

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁירָה, וְלֹא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה.
phrases.english: it is valid, but it does not count for the owner as his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אָשָׁם בֶּן שָׁנָה וֶהֱבִיאוֹ בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the proof for רבי יוחנן's claim about רבי שמעון
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds something unfit in itself gets no קדושת הגוף
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an אשם brought at the wrong age (the תנא קמא's part)

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the wrong-age אשם is not holy at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says these animals are not holy at all. This proves that for him, something unfit in itself gets no קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: they are not holy at all.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the proof. רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא and says the wrong-age אשם never became holy in its body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal of the wrong age cannot be offered as that אשם, and רבי שמעון says it is not holy at all. This matches רבי יוחנן's rule: for רבי שמעון, something unfit in itself does not get קדושת הגוף. The same is true of the female set aside for an אשם, so it may be sold without a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: They themselves are not holy at all

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון holds that holiness of the body cannot rest on an animal that is unfit to be offered. That is why the מיגו does not help in the case of the female אשם.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עַצְמָן אֵינָן קְדוֹשִׁין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: they themselves are not holy at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עַצְמָן אֵינָן קְדוֹשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof from the ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ruling in the ברייתא that a wrong-age אשם is not holy at all

steps.title: A young animal is unfit, yet רבי שמעון calls it holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from the case of an animal that is too young to be offered. רבי שמעון holds that it is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about an animal whose time has not yet come? It is not fit to be offered, and still רבי שמעון said it is holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from Step 14, that for רבי שמעון something unfit in itself gets no קדושת הגוף. It brings a case where רבי שמעון does give holiness to something unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר זמן is an animal too young to be offered, so it cannot go on the מזבח right now. If רבי שמעון still calls it holy, then being unfit does not block holiness for him. This seems to contradict the explanation רבי יוחנן gave.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal 'missing time': too young to be offered yet
That is not fit (to be offered)
Holy, has the status of a קרבן
But look at this case (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But there is an animal whose time has not yet come,
phrases.notes: This means an animal that is too young to be offered, for example one less than eight days old.

phrases.english: which is not fit,
and רבי שמעון said that it is holy!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי מְחוּסַּר זְמַן, דְּלָא חֲזֵי, וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּקָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle that the proof in Steps 15-16 had just backed up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that for רבי שמעון, whatever is unfit in itself gets no קדושת הגוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מחוסר זמן is unfit, yet רבי שמעון calls it holy. So being unfit does not stop holiness.

steps.title: A young animal will be fit soon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a young animal is different, because it will become fit on its own very soon.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal whose time has not come is different, because it will be fit tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן's rule. It says a young animal does not really count as 'unfit', since it will be fit for the מזבח soon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates two kinds of 'unfit'. An animal that is unfit only for a short time counts as fit, because time alone will fix it. So רבי שמעון's rule about unfit things does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different
Tomorrow, meaning at a later time

phrases.english: An animal whose time has not come is different,
since it will be fit tomorrow.
phrases.notes: Not literally tomorrow. He means it will become fit on its own after a little time passes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: being unfit only for a while is not the same as being truly unfit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A young animal is unfit, so it should get no holiness according to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A young animal will soon be fit, so it counts as fit and can become holy.

steps.title: The wrong-age אשם will also be fit later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer: an אשם brought too young will also be fit after a year, yet רבי שמעון says it is not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, an אשם that must be two years old but was brought at one year old will be fit in another year! So why isn't it holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of Step 18. It points to the אשם case from Steps 15-16, which also 'will be fit later'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16, רבי שמעון said an אשם brought at the wrong age is not holy at all. But that animal will grow into the right age in a year, just like a young animal grows past eight days. So 'it will be fit later' cannot be the real reason for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your answer is right, then...)
Guilt offering
In its second year (two years old)
In its first year (one year old)

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: אָשָׁם בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם וֶהֱבִיאוֹ בֶּן שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: a guilt offering that must be in its second year, and he brought it in its first year,
it will be fit in another year!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אָשָׁם בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם וֶהֱבִיאוֹ בֶּן שָׁנָה, הָא חֲזֵי לְשָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 18 by pointing to the case in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a young animal is holy because it will be fit later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wrong-age אשם will also be fit later, yet רבי שמעון says it is not holy. So 'fit later' cannot explain the difference.

steps.title: The real reason: learned from a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'fit tomorrow' idea. It says רבי שמעון makes a young animal holy because he learns it from a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רבי שמעון's reason for an animal whose time has not come: he learns it from a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of Step 17. רבי שמעון's ruling on young animals comes from a special comparison to a בכור, not from general logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the earlier answer is being dropped. Now the young animal's holiness comes from a special source, a learning from בכור. So it is an exception, and the general rule from Step 14 stays in place. This is why the wrong-age אשם still gets no holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer)
The reason
He learns it (derives it from another source)
A firstborn animal, holy from birth

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of רבי שמעון
regarding an animal whose time has not come:
that he learns it from a firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּמְחוּסַּר זְמַן, דְּיָלֵיף לֵיהּ מִבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of Step 18, which Step 19 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: a special learning from בכור makes the young animal an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The young animal is holy because it will be fit soon.
steps.terutzMaskana: The young animal is holy only because of a special learning from בכור. The general rule for unfit things stays.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying a young animal is fit. It is still unfit right now. It is holy only because of the special comparison to a בכור.

steps.title: A ברייתא compares a young animal to a בכור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי שמעון shows that a young animal is like a בכור: holy before its time, and offered after its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן יהודה said in the name of רבי שמעון: an animal whose time has not come goes into the pen to be tithed. It is like a בכור. A בכור is holy before its time and is offered after its time. So too, an animal whose time has not come is holy before its time and is offered after its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what Step 20 said: רבי שמעון really does learn the young animal's law from a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy the moment it is born, even though it cannot be offered until it is eight days old. The ברייתא says a young animal is the same: it can become holy now (for example through מעשר בהמה) and be offered later. This proves the young animal's holiness comes from the בכור comparison, not from a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal pen
To be tithed (מַעֲשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, the tenth animal becomes holy)
Before its time (before it is old enough to be offered)
Is offered on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, something unfit in itself gets no קדושת הגוף. A young animal is a special exception, learned from a בכור: holy now, offered later.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
An animal whose time has not come enters the pen to be tithed,
and it is like a firstborn:
just as a firstborn is holy before its time
and is offered after its time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מְחוּסַּר זְמַן קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ
phrases.english: so too, an animal whose time has not come is holy before its time
and is offered after its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 20 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון learns the holiness of a מחוסר זמן from בכור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון, comparing a young animal to a בכור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 14. The young animal is holy only because of a special learning, so the general rule for unfit things still holds.

steps.title: New ברייתא: a female set aside for an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא about someone who sets aside a female animal for his עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: one who sets aside a female animal for his עולה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts quoting a ברייתא about a female animal set aside for an עולה, and the ruling will come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be a male, so a female is not fit to be offered as one. This is another case of something unfit in itself, which connects to the argument about רבי שמעון. The ברייתא's ruling has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside an animal as holy
A female animal
A burnt offering, which must be a male

phrases.english: The Sages taught: one who sets aside a female for his burnt offering

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא that goes back to the topic of unfit animals and holiness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. The ברייתא only sets up the case of a female set aside for an עולה.
